answer: Each identity claims one summit transect marked by cedar stakes and locks a 70-credit bond. Each epoch it files a snow-depth reading and an inlet gauge reading for that transect. An auditor recomputes the melt total from the transect table; a mismatch, reused stake, or copied reading burns the bond. The first fee is 33 credits, the kth 33+7(k-1), the 1000th 7026, so 1000 fakes pay 3,529,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-survey ring fails because rented readings carry the wrong key and a transect accepts only its stakes. An honest surveyor pays 33 once and recovers the bond after a clean audit.
